title: The Week That Was
gist: A Lawfare weekly roundup surfacing several investable legal-risk threads: the Pentagon taking equity stakes in critical mineral and defense technology companies without clear authority, data center colocation placing U.S. AI servers alongside Chinese tenants, a proposal to restrict U.S. sales of AI training environments to China, and a legally shaky suspension of phase two of the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program. It also carries a 25th-anniversary reassessment of the post-9/11 homeland security and data-sharing apparatus.

themes.theme: Pentagon equity stakes in critical minerals

insights.claim: The Department of Defense has recently taken several equity stakes in critical mineral and defense technology companies without clearly stating the legal authority it is relying on to do so.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: State-backed equity is becoming a real capital source for critical-minerals and defense-tech names; watch which issuers disclose DoD stakes and how they justify them.
insights.quote: the Department of Defense has recently acquired several equity stakes in critical mineral and defense technology companies, but has not clearly stated under what authority it is doing so
insights.locator: Benjamin Press explained that the Department

insights.claim: The Pentagon's equity investments are likely resting on stretched readings of existing statutory authorities that do not clearly hold up, creating legal fragility around those deals.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Legal challenge risk is an unpriced overhang on companies whose valuations were re-rated by a DoD equity stake.
insights.quote: the Pentagon is likely relying on stretched readings of its existing authorities that don’t clearly hold up

insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog

themes.theme: Data center colocation as an espionage surface

insights.claim: The U.S. data center buildout relies heavily on colocation, in which multiple companies house their servers inside the same physical facility.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Physical tenancy structure, not just chip supply, is becoming a diligence item for AI infrastructure and data center landlord exposure.

insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Tenant-screening rules or forced physical separation would raise data center costs and favor operators with dedicated single-tenant hyperscale capacity.

insights.claim: Selective Availability, the U.S. policy limiting access to early GPS technology, functioned as an effective pacing mechanism but was made obsolete by technical advances, commercial-use pressure, and military modernization.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A historical base rate for how fast technology controls decay: expect AI safeguards to have short half-lives once commercial demand builds.

themes.theme: CMMC pause and defense industrial base exposure

insights.claim: New Department of Defense memos suspend phase two of the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A near-term reprieve in compliance spend for defense suppliers and for vendors selling CMMC readiness services.

insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Compliance relief may prove temporary; suppliers that stand down certification work risk a rushed and costly restart.

themes.theme: Post-9/11 security architecture reassessed at 25 years

insights.claim: A former Secretary of Homeland Security has proposed collapsing the patchwork U.S. homeland security system into a single Cabinet-level agency combining law enforcement, counterterrorism, cybersecurity, and aviation security, while keeping certain immigration and disaster response functions separate.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A serious reorganization would redraw the procurement map for screening, security and cyber vendors selling into DHS components.
insights.locator: As part of Lawfare's Sept. 11 essay collection

insights.claim: The Department of Homeland Security drifted from a border security and counterterrorism initiative, to domestic threat monitoring, and finally into a sprawling immigration apparatus, with each step individually justifiable but the cumulative result being lost mission focus and eroded public support.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A template for how agencies with open-ended mandates accrete mission until they face restructuring risk, which reshuffles the budget lines vendors depend on.
insights.quote: together they gradually resulted in a DHS that has lost sight of its original mission and its remaining public support
insights.locator: Paul Rosenzweig traced how the Department

insights.claim: Today's automated immigration enforcement originates in data-sharing approaches first conceived after 9/11, and systems built to prevent intelligence oversights have quietly expanded into a massive ecosystem holding data on millions of Americans.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Government data-integration is a durable growth market and simultaneously the most likely target of a future privacy backlash or litigation wave.
insights.quote: systems once designed to prevent intelligence oversights have since quietly expanded into a massive ecosystem of data on millions of Americans
insights.locator: Chinmayi Sharma analyzed the origins

insights.claim: Post-9/11 U.S.-EU agreements greatly expanded transatlantic data sharing, created an expectation of mutual aid, and solidified the EU as the legal body to negotiate with on counterterrorism matters.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: The EU-as-counterparty precedent underpins the cross-border data transfer regimes that global tech and financial firms still depend on.
insights.quote: the agreements greatly expanded U.S.-EU data sharing, created the expectation of mutual aid, and solidified the EU as a legal body to negotiate with
insights.locator: Kenneth Propp reviewed how, following 9/11

insights.claim: The government backed out of plea agreements reached with 9/11 defendants detained at Guantanamo Bay, and advocates are urging the Supreme Court to review whether the government can lawfully withdraw from such agreements.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A cert grant would be a visible test of whether government contractual commitments can be unilaterally unwound.
insights.quote: they urged the Supreme Court to review whether the government can withdraw from the agreement
insights.locator: Michel Paradis and Nick Lewin discussed

insights.claim: A judge denied the government's motion to dismiss a suit seeking information on U.S. international agreements, allowing litigation over the State Department's failure to release that documentation to proceed.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Discovery into undisclosed international agreements could surface commitments that affect trade, defense or sanctions expectations.

insights.claim: Litigation is actively under way over the administration's targeting of mail voting, alongside other suits against the administration.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Election-mechanics litigation is a live political-risk item to track ahead of the next federal election cycle.
insights.quote: developments in President Trump’s targeting of mail voting
insights.locator: developments in President Trump’s targeting of mail voting

insights.claim: Reporting built on a review of thousands of criminal cases plus interviews with National Guard members and D.C. officials is being used to test whether the Guard's domestic deployment in Washington is operating lawfully.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Empirical case-level evidence, not just legal argument, is now shaping the domestic-deployment debate and its likely judicial outcome.
insights.locator: Orpett sat down with Brad Heath

insights.claim: Cities act both as laboratories of democracy and as backstops against democratic backsliding, which is why autocrats target mayors.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Municipal governance resilience is an underrated variable in country and political-risk models.
insights.quote: cities are both “laboratories of democracy” and backstops against democratic backsliding

insights.claim: Algorithmic disgorgement, a remedy first used by the Federal Trade Commission, is expanding as a tool for addressing algorithmic harms.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Model-deletion as a remedy is a tail legal risk for AI firms trained on contested data; watch FTC remedy language in consent orders.
